question: step 7b (split live ranges at loop boundaries): how much of the suite's spilling is a value live across a loop, unused inside it, spilled everywhere?
method: temporary diagnostic in Codegen.Allocate (FPR_ALLOC_DEBUG=1, cold unit caches): per spilled value, accesses at loop depth > 0 vs outside, and whether its interval crosses a loop block; raw profiles kept out of tree

a64.note: one per function: floatcmp's loop, sha's extend/blocks/rounds/sha1Rounds, exactGo/untilGo/scanFrom; every affected access is outside the loop, i.e. cold

x64.note: the shape is much more common under x64's 12-register budget, but still entirely outside the loops

verdict: 7b's split never changes a hot loop body: the value is unused inside, so spilled-or-split the loop is identical; the entire benefit is a handful of cold loads/stores per function. Not worth edge move resolution now. The form with real potential is call-boundary splitting (a spill lasting only across the call that forced it) for loops whose calls force the callee-saved budget, but the suite's hot loops have no such case: pingpong's loops are call-heavy and spill-free, sha's 23 spills in rounds are pure over-pressure with no call in the body — that wants fewer live values (plan step 4.3 cross-block sharing), not splitting
